analysis: Derivational complexity of the 162 terminating rules - 140 linear, 14 quadratic, 4 exponential, 4 non-rational (the aab -> ba class); simple floor-quadratic or 2^(n-1)-1 closed forms for 54 of 55 symmetry classes. Among length-preserving rules with |l| >= 2 only ab <-> ba attains floor(n^2/4), consistent with Bertrand's theorem.

falsification: A rule whose D_max admits no over-determined recurrence, or a growth class other than linear/quadratic/exponential.

hypothesis: H-C04-G: every terminating rule in the family has derivational complexity D(n) = max over words of length n of the longest derivation that is linear, quadratic or exponential, and D(n) is given by a linear recurrence (rational generating function).
methodology: Exact min/max derivation lengths per word from the acyclic derivation graph; D_max(n), D_min(n); minimal linear recurrence (Berlekamp-Massey, over-determined) and the moduli/multiplicities of its characteristic roots give the growth class. Rules are grouped by the symmetries reversal and letter exchange.
question: How long can derivations of a terminating one-rule system be, as a function of the length of the start word, and which growth classes occur?
